To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the combination of a compiler infrastructure and a runtime system for a PGAS language can produce programs with performance comparable with MPI programs and good scalability up to hundreds-of-thousands of processors, 2) the runtime system design is scalable and efficient, and 3) the compiler infrastructure simplifies parallel loop code and improves the performance of shared memory accesses.

the UPC programming model is scalable to hundreds of thousands or more of processors and that the combination of a compiler and a runtime system can produce UPC programs with performance comparable or better than that of efficient MPI-based implementations of the same application.

a compiler for UPC can generate code with performance comparable to hand-optimized MPI programs, and that a runtime system for UPC that uses a distributed directory-based approach can maintain shared memory consistency efficiently in a massively parallel machine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of a scalable run time system for UPC, a parallel language that supports a global address space, and an optimizing compiler that can produce efficient code for UPC.
the design and implementation issues of a scalable UPC run-time system and optimizing compiler
the design, implementation, and evaluation of scalable programming environments and tools for parallel programming.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UPC is competitive with MPI in performance and scalability, and that it provides the programmer with an easier and more intuitive programming model.
our compiler and runtime system provide a scalable programming environment for UPC on distributed-memory machines.
UPC is an attractive programming model for large-scale machines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UPC can be used to develop efficient parallel applications for large-scale machines.
we have shown the viability of a PGAS language as a high-level programming model for a large-scale machine.

we have shown that UPC is a scalable programming language for distributed memory machines, and that our compiler and runtime system are effective in producing UPC programs that perform as well as MPI programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of a compiler that can exploit locality information and a runtime system that can provide scalable shared memory consistency can produce performance comparable to MPI on distributed-memory machines.
a combination of compiler and runtime system optimizations can provide performance comparable to MPI on a large distributed-memory machine.

the combination of an optimizing compiler infrastructure with an efficient runtime system can produce UPC programs that scale well on large distributed memory machines and that are as fast as MPI programs.
